question: Why does nobody get herd protection against tetanus, however many of their neighbours are vaccinated?
answer: Because tetanus does not pass from person to person. Its spores live in soil, dust and manure and enter through a wound, so a vaccinated neighbour blocks no route to anyone else. Herd protection needs a chain of infection to break. With tetanus there is no chain: each unvaccinated person faces the soil alone.
move: Before counting on the crowd to shield you, check how the danger actually travels.
ask: Which risk am I assuming other people's choices cover for me, when only my own choice can?
